title: Konza plans KSh 28.2 billion park to make medicines in Kenya
dek: A feasibility study is under way for a 200 acre biopharma hub at Konza Technopolis.
body: Kenya is studying plans for its first biopharma and life sciences park at Konza Technopolis, a project Invest Kenya values at about US$217 million, roughly KSh 28.2 billion.
The 200 acre park aims to attract seven to ten major pharmaceutical companies and cut the country's reliance on imported medicines.

Apifa Biotech has secured a grant from Swedfund to pay for a feasibility study, with the Konza Technopolis Development Authority as the public partner. The National Treasury cleared the project to move into its development phase in April 2026.

No construction date or job figures have been announced yet; those will depend on the study. Konza CEO John Paul Okwiri described the plan as turning the technopolis into an emerging centre for life sciences.
For Machakos and Makueni, where Konza sits, a working pharmaceutical park would mean skilled jobs and new business for suppliers, transport and housing.
q: Konza has been promised for years. Do you think this project will finally bring jobs to the area?
